recipe.name: hb1603_dive_analysis
recipe.description: Pooled HDBSCAN clustering of 13 HB1603 sperm whale dives with per-dive SVCodes, seabed masked on Sv.

nodes.label: inputs.file_time_start
nodes.description: Lower bound of the catalogue query. Deliberately wider than the cruise, which runs 2016-06-27 to 2016-08-25, so the window states an intent rather than a measurement and does not need editing if the catalogue gains a file at either end. It must stay fixed once a scan has been cached: it is a query param, so moving it re-runs every instance.

nodes.label: inputs.file_time_end
nodes.description: Upper bound of the catalogue query. See file_time_start.

nodes.label: inputs.cruise_name
nodes.description: CRUISE_NAME filter for the NCEI catalogue query.

nodes.label: inputs.max_scan_bytes
nodes.description: Leading bytes read per raw object. See the note above before lowering.

nodes.label: inputs.cal_input_folder
nodes.description: Manufacturer .cal files.

nodes.label: inputs.cruise_id
nodes.description: Recorded in every generated single-channel file.

nodes.label: inputs.record_author
nodes.description: Recorded as the author of every generated single-channel file.

nodes.label: inputs.match_tolerances
nodes.description: Per-field tolerances for matching a raw channel to a calibration file, merged over the matcher's exact defaults. See the note below on why transmit_power is widened for HB1603.

nodes.label: inputs.sonar_model
nodes.description: Sonar model string for echopype.

nodes.label: inputs.crop_max_range_m
nodes.description: Range ceiling applied per file. Every consumer shares it: change it and the whole survey Sv is recomputed.

nodes.label: inputs.ping_time_bin
nodes.description: Ping-time bin of the per-dive grid. Level 2b widens each dive window to whole bins of this width, level 3 grids on it, and level 5 counts one bin of this length per ping in the duration tables.
Turn the NEFSC dive configs into recipe windows.
Query an NCEI acoustic data catalog for file listings within a time window. Returns a list of result records (file metadata), not the files themselves.

params.name: file_time_start
params.description: ISO 8601 start of window, e.g. '2016-07-25T20:58'

params.name: file_time_end
params.description: ISO 8601 end of window

params.name: filters
params.description: Key-value filters applied to NCEI metadata (e.g. CRUISE_NAME)

params.name: file_names
params.description: Keep only these files, matched on the D{date}-T{time} stamp in the name, so a bare D20160725-T205832.raw finds the archive's HB1603_L1- form and the reverse. Applied after the time window, client side, in catalogue order. A name the query did not return raises rather than silently shrinking the result. Wire it from a planning step, for example ${plan_dives.raw_files}, to map a per-file chain over an analysis's files alone. Empty keeps everything.

outputs.name: ncei_results
outputs.description: List of NCEI file metadata records (dicts) matching the query

outputs.name: query_label
outputs.description: Readable, folder-safe slug derived from the query parameters. Intended to be passed to download_ncei_data so that each query writes into its own subfolder under output_dir.

outputs.name: raw_urls
outputs.description:
Public HTTPS URL of each record's .raw object, in record order. For steps that read a file in place rather than downloading it, such as read_raw_file_config with max_scan_bytes: map over this and each instance range-reads the leading bytes of one file, with nothing transferred whole and nothing left on disk.
Plain strings, so a mapped instance is content-addressed by its URL and dedupes across runs the same way a raw file path does. Built rather than probed, so a record whose object is not stored as <key>.raw fails on read instead of costing a HEAD request per file.

nodes.description:
Read ONE raw file's channel configuration from its datagram headers.
The fan-out unit of the calibration raw scan. Map it over initial_setup.raw_file_paths with checkpoint: always and each file becomes its own cache entry, so a run interrupted at file 400 of 500 keeps the 399 already scanned. Pair it with record_raw_file_configs, which collects the results into the survey's raw_file_configs.yaml.

params.name: raw_file_path
params.description: One .raw file. May be a local path or a remote fsspec URL, which is downloaded to local scratch, read, and deleted before this step returns. Normally wired to ${_item}. Not fingerprinted, because the mapped item already content-addresses the instance.

params.name: verify_start_time
params.description: If true, EK80 files are additionally read with the full SimradFileReader to verify metadata_start_time, which is slower. The default single pass scan is enough for channel configuration.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Print per-file progress. Worth setting false on a long fan-out, where one banner per file buries the rest of the log.

params.name: max_scan_bytes
params.description:
Ceiling on how many leading bytes of a remote EK60 or EK80 file may be read in place of transferring it whole. The scan starts at min(8 MiB, this) and doubles up to this cap, stopping as soon as the configuration settles every channel, so a file that settles early pays only the small read and the local prefix grows in place rather than being re-read from zero.
Size it for the deepest configuration in the survey. Too low is expensive, not wrong: a file that never settles is read whole.
EK80: CW files settle within a fraction of a MiB; FM files sit behind much larger RAW3 payloads and scale with file size, so a survey of ~1 GiB FM files needs a cap in the tens of MiB.
EK60 settles far earlier, and the cap doubles as the starting read, so setting it to 1 MiB turns a cruise-wide scan into one small read per file. Measured on HB1603 (52 MB files, five channels), the configuration settles at 256 KiB. Do not be tempted lower on the strength of the channel list alone: at 64 KiB every channel is already listed and looks complete, but three of the five carry CON0's configured 2000 W rather than the 500, 300 and 750 W actually transmitted. The step guards against that by requiring one RAW0 datagram per channel before it trusts a prefix, so a too-small cap costs a whole-file read rather than wrong calibration.
Because a prefix cannot measure them, the per-file datagram counts and gps_data come back null; last_ping_time is recovered from the file's tail. Leave unset for the whole-file read, which is also what local files and verify_start_time always get.

outputs.name: file_config
outputs.description: This file's channel configuration: filename, metadata_start_time, and one entry per channel. Null when the instrument type cannot be detected, and record_raw_file_configs drops those entries.

nodes.description:
Collect per-file channel configurations into the survey's raw config file.
The fan-in half of the raw scan. Drops the files that could not be read, sorts the rest by metadata_start_time, and writes raw_file_configs/raw_file_configs.yaml under the calibration output directory. Declare it with collect on the scan step's file_config output.

inputs.name: file_configs
inputs.description: The collected per-file configurations, normally wired to the mapped read_raw_file_config step's file_config output. Null entries are dropped.

params.name: output_base
params.description: Root directory the calibration artifacts are written under. Normally wired to initial_setup's calibration_output_dir.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Print a summary of what was recorded.

outputs.name: raw_file_configs
outputs.description: The saved configurations, sorted by metadata_start_time. Pass to build_calibration_mapping so it need not re-read them from disk.

outputs.name: frequencies
outputs.description: Sorted unique channel frequencies in Hz. Sets the channel order for EK60 (.cal) calibration data, and is optional for EK80.

outputs.name: raw_configs_path
outputs.description: Full path of the raw_file_configs.yaml that was written. Wire it into build_calibration_mapping for the ordering dependency.

nodes.description:
Convert manufacturer calibration files to standardized single-channel files.
Parses the EK60 .cal or EK80 .xml files in the calibration input folder, validates them against the standardized schema, and writes one .yaml per channel into single_channel_calibration_files/ under the calibration output directory. These per-channel files are what NCEI archives.
The parse is skipped when standardization.fingerprint.json shows the same manufacturer files already produced the files that are there. That sidecar answers to the manufacturer folder, so deleting a single-channel file does not bring it back, which is what the mapping step's "error" conflict workflow relies on.

inputs.name: frequencies
inputs.description: Unique channel frequencies in Hz, normally from record_raw_file_configs. Sets the channel order for EK60 (.cal) data and is optional for EK80. Recovered from the saved raw_file_configs.yaml when omitted.

params.name: cal_input_folder
params.description: Folder of manufacturer calibration files (.cal for EK60, .xml for EK80). May be a remote fsspec URL, which is downloaded whole to local scratch for the duration of the parse.

params.name: output_base
params.description: Root directory the calibration artifacts are written under. Normally wired to initial_setup's calibration_output_dir.

params.name: cruise_id
params.description: Cruise identifier recorded in every generated single-channel file (e.g. "HB2407"), so a standardized file stays traceable to the survey it came from.

params.name: record_author
params.description: Name recorded as the author of every generated single-channel file. Part of the provenance the standardized format carries, not something the calculation uses.

params.name: short_filenames
params.description: Use compact names for the generated single-channel files. Set false for longer, more descriptive names. The names become the calibration keys the mapping is built from, so this participates in the reuse fingerprint.

params.name: overwrite
params.description: Re-parse and rewrite even when the sidecar says the existing files are current, forcing a clean rebuild of the single-channel folder.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Print the parsed parameters and the files written.

params.name: override_channels
params.description:
Write these channels as the single-channel files instead of parsing the manufacturer files. Same shape as the single_channel_data output: omit an entry to discard that channel, and edit values in place to correct them. This is how a reviewed and edited set of channels comes back from a caller that has no access to the folder.
_calibration_file_key is ignored on input, because filenames are re-derived from the supplied values and an edit can therefore rename a file. The channels are validated against the standardized schema before anything is written, and the folder is cleared first so a discarded channel leaves no orphan behind for the mapping to match. Folded into the standardization fingerprint, so changing them rewrites the folder, and a later run that parses the manufacturer files again clears what an override wrote rather than mapping both sets.

outputs.name: single_channel_dir
outputs.description: Folder the single-channel files were written to. Wire it into build_calibration_mapping for the ordering dependency.

outputs.name: channel_count
outputs.description: Number of single-channel calibration files in that folder.

outputs.name: skipped
outputs.description: True when the existing files were reused because the manufacturer files had not changed.

outputs.name: single_channel_data
outputs.description: The standardized channels as data: {"channels": [...]}, one entry per single-channel file, each carrying the _calibration_file_key that the mapping is built on. Produced on the fresh parse, the reuse path and an override alike, so a caller can review the channels without reading the folder. Plain JSON types only, so it checkpoints as JSON rather than a pickle and stays eligible for the shared survey cache.

nodes.description:
Match each raw channel to its calibration data and save the mapping files.
Loads the raw file configurations and the standardized single-channel files, runs the matching algorithm, moves aside any calibration file no raw channel matched, resolves conflicts, writes mapping_files/channel_mapping.yaml, calibration_configurations.yaml and calibration_provenance.yaml, and verifies the result.
Reads the single-channel files from disk rather than taking them as data. The mapping keys are those files' names, which only the on-disk loader attaches, and this step rewrites that folder.
Mark it regenerate: always in a recipe. Its real product is the files on disk, and a hand-deleted single-channel file cannot change a cache key computed before the run, so a cache hit would return the dictionaries without re-reading the folder. The step is cheap: a few small local YAML reads and the matcher.

inputs.name: raw_file_configs
inputs.description: The raw file configurations to map, normally from record_raw_file_configs. Read from the saved raw_file_configs.yaml under output_base when omitted.

params.name: output_base
params.description: Root directory the calibration artifacts are written under. Normally wired to initial_setup's calibration_output_dir.

params.name: single_channel_dir
params.description: Folder of standardized single-channel files. Defaults to single_channel_calibration_files/ under output_base. Wire it to the standardization step's single_channel_dir output for the ordering dependency. Not fingerprinted, because a step-output reference is still an unresolved placeholder when cache keys are computed; use regenerate: always instead.

params.name: raw_configs_path
params.description: Path of the saved raw_file_configs.yaml. Defaults to raw_file_configs/raw_file_configs.yaml under output_base, and is only consulted when raw_file_configs is not supplied.

params.name: conflict_resolution
params.description: What to do when one raw channel matches several calibration files. "error" (the default) lists the conflicts and stops, so you delete the unwanted single-channel file and re-run. "interactive" prompts on the terminal, and raises before any file is moved when the run has no interactive input. "report" neither raises nor prompts: it returns the conflicts on the conflicts output and writes no mapping file, which is the mode for a caller with no terminal that will present the choices and run the step again with calibration_choices.

params.name: calibration_choices
params.description: Conflict decisions supplied up front, mapping a conflict id from a previous run's conflicts output to the calibration key to keep. A list of candidate keys in place of one key averages them: the average is written as a new single-channel file with is_averaged set, the conflict's channels are mapped to it, and the candidates it was made from are set aside. Only calibrations of the same transducer, at the same settings and with the same sphere, can be averaged. Applied in every conflict_resolution mode before that mode's handler runs, so a partial map resolves what it covers and leaves the rest to be reported, prompted for, or raised on. An unknown conflict id, a key that is not one of that conflict's candidates, or candidates that cannot be averaged, is an error, and nothing is changed.

params.name: tolerances
params.description:
Per-field match tolerances, merged over the matcher's defaults so a dict naming only one field widens only that field. The defaults are exact for frequency, frequency_start, frequency_end and transmit_power (1 Hz / 1 W) and 1e-6 s for transmit_duration_nominal, because a calibration is formally valid only for the configuration it was measured at.
Widening one is a scientific decision, not a convenience: a channel that matches only under a widened tolerance was calibrated at a different setting than it is being applied to, and the resulting gain and sa_correction carry a bias of that difference. Every override is reported on the terminal. Reach for it when a survey changed a setting mid-cruise and no calibration exists for the other side of the change, and record why in the recipe.

params.name: unmapped_channels
params.description: The policy the extract_standardized_cal_params step that consumes this mapping runs with, "warn" or "error". Informational only: it changes nothing about the matching, and only lets the provenance report state what actually happened to an unmatched channel instead of listing both possibilities. Set it to the same value that step uses, or leave it out and the report says the outcome is decided downstream.

params.name: cruise_id
params.description: Recorded in the provenance report when given.

params.name: record_author
params.description: Recorded as the author of any record averaged while resolving conflicts. When omitted, the averaged calibrations' author is kept if they share one.

params.name: keep_unused
params.description: Move calibration files no raw channel matched into unused_calibration_files/ instead of deleting them. They are the evidence when a channel comes out unmapped.

params.name: short_filenames
params.description: Remap the returned dictionaries to compact calibration keys when they are not already the single-channel file names, and give averaged records compact keys. Should match the setting the single-channel files were written with.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Print the mapping summary, preview, and verification results.

outputs.name: mapping_dict
outputs.description: Maps each raw file's channels to their calibration key, keyed by filename then channel_id. Feed to extract_standardized_cal_params.

outputs.name: calibration_dict
outputs.description: Parsed standardized calibration data keyed by calibration key. Holds the values themselves. Feed to extract_standardized_cal_params.

outputs.name: missing_params
outputs.description: Calibration keys mapped to the required parameters they are missing. An empty dict means every required parameter is present.

outputs.name: unused_files
outputs.description: Names of single-channel calibration files the mapping does not reference, including the ones this run moved aside. An empty list means every calibration file matched a raw channel, so a non-empty one is the signal that a channel went unmapped. Under "report" no mapping exists to check against, so this carries only the files the run moved aside.

outputs.name: provenance
outputs.description:
Per-channel account of what calibration was applied over which stretch of the cruise, and why. Each channel carries segments, one per run of raw files that behaved the same way, with a time range, the raw and calibration settings behind it, and an outcome: the calibration was applied, it was applied only because a tolerance was widened, or nothing matched and the channel fell back or stopped the run. A cruise of thousands of files reports as a handful of segments per channel.
JSON-safe, so a server can hand it to a client without reading the file off disk. The same content is written to mapping_files/calibration_provenance.yaml.
Complete whatever happens downstream: the mapping stage sees every file in the catalogue, so this covers the whole cruise even when the per-file tier that consumes the mapping is still running or stopped early.

outputs.name: provenance_path
outputs.description: Where the provenance report was written as YAML, under mapping_files/ in output_base.

outputs.name: conflicts
outputs.description: Unresolved multiple-match conflicts, keyed by a stable conflict id. Each carries the candidate calibration keys, a summary of every candidate, the raw files and channel ids it affects, and distinguishing_fields naming what actually differs between the candidates. That list excludes the fields two calibration records differ in by construction, such as the source filename and the created timestamp, so it names only what a reviewer has to weigh. It is empty when the candidates match everywhere it matters. Only populated under conflict_resolution "report"; empty when the mapping completed. A non-empty value means no mapping file was written, so feed the choices back as calibration_choices and run the step again.

outputs.name: single_channel_data
outputs.description: {"channels": [...]}, the standardized channels the mapping was built from plus any record averaged from several of them, each carrying its _calibration_file_key. Every key in mapping_dict names one of them, so this, not the standardization step's payload, is what to hand to save_calibration_archive once an average has been chosen. JSON-safe.

nodes.description:
Open raw echosounder files with echopype and write each file as an intermediate per-file store. Returns a list of store-path strings for file-backed formats, or a list of in-memory EchoData objects when intermediate_format is "none". This is the future map_over target for parallel per-file processing. NOTE: use intermediate_format "netcdf" (default) or "none". The "zarr" option is not recommended; see the intermediate_format parameter description below.
The per-file conversion is echopype.open_raw, and sonar_model, include_bot, and use_swap are forwarded to it. Around that call this step adds remote file staging, .bot companion handling, and writing each result to an intermediate store.

inputs.name: raw_file_paths
inputs.description: Paths to .raw files to open. Entries may be local paths or remote fsspec URLs (e.g. gs://bucket/survey/file.raw). Each remote file is downloaded to a local scratch directory, converted, and the local copy deleted before the next file is fetched, so the machine only ever holds ~1 raw file at a time. Bucket objects are never modified or deleted.

params.name: sonar_model
params.description: Sonar model string recognized by echopype (e.g. 'EK60', 'EK80')

params.name: include_bot
params.description: Include bottom-detection (.bot) data if available

params.name: intermediate_format
params.description:
Intermediate store format written to exe_temp/data between the read_raw and combine_raw steps. Supported values: "netcdf" (default), "zarr", "none".
"netcdf" (default, recommended): each raw file is written as a temporary .nc file, reopened, and combined. After combining, all EchoData groups are rechunked to a single uniform chunk so the downstream zarr v2 checkpoint write (combine_raw with checkpoint: always) always succeeds.
"none": all EchoData objects are kept in memory with no temp files. Use when the full dataset fits comfortably in RAM.
"zarr": each raw file is written as a temporary zarr store (zarr_format=2, matching the checkpoint writer) and reopened lazily for combining. Unlike netcdf, zarr stores can live on remote object storage (e.g. a GCS bucket) by passing a gs:// --temp-dir, which is the intended path for surveys too large to stage on local disk. Combined with gs:// raw_file_paths, local disk usage stays at roughly one raw file for the whole run.

params.name: use_swap
params.description: Passed to echopype open_raw as use_swap. "auto" (default) triggers per-file swap when the expanded data would exceed ~40% of total RAM.

outputs.name: raw_stores
outputs.description: Store path strings (zarr/netcdf) written to exe_temp/data, or in-memory EchoData objects when intermediate_format is "none".

nodes.description:
Lazily open per-file intermediate stores (zarr or netcdf paths) produced by read_raw_files, or combine in-memory EchoData objects (none mode), into a single combined EchoData object. Mark this step checkpoint: always in your recipe so the checkpoint system writes the combined output once and reuses it on subsequent runs.
The reading and the combine itself are echopype.open_converted and echopype.combine_echodata. Around them this step adds store-path handling, input ordering, and the ping_time chunking of the combined result.

inputs.name: raw_stores
inputs.description: Store paths (zarr/netcdf strings) or in-memory EchoData objects

params.name: ping_time_chunk
params.description: Target chunk length along ping_time for the combined EchoData, which directly sets the chunking of the downstream zarr checkpoint. Larger values mean fewer, bigger objects: faster remote (gs://) checkpoint writes and fewer read requests, at the cost of more RAM per computed chunk and coarser lazy-read granularity for windowed access. 1000 is a balanced default; try 2000-4000 for bucket-backed caches if the combined checkpoint write is slow and memory allows.

outputs.name: echodata
outputs.description: Combined echopype EchoData object

nodes.description: Extract calibration parameters (gain, sa-correction, EBA) and environmental parameters (sound speed, absorption) from standardized calibration files, cross-referenced against the EchoData object for channel alignment.

inputs.name: calibration_dict
inputs.description: Parsed standardized calibration data keyed by calibration key, from generate_standardized_cal_mapping. Holds the values themselves.

inputs.name: mapping_dict
inputs.description: Raw channel to calibration key mapping, from generate_standardized_cal_mapping. Says which entry of calibration_dict belongs to each channel of each file.

inputs.name: echodata
inputs.description: EchoData whose channel labels the calibration values are aligned to, normally the combined object from combine_raw_files. The outputs are keyed by that object's channels, so they can be passed straight to compute_sv.

params.name: raw_file_path
params.description: Path to the specific raw file whose channel mapping should be selected from mapping_dict (matched by basename). Wire this to ${_item} in a per-file map_over chain so each instance picks its own file's calibration mapping instead of defaulting to the first file in the survey. Leave unset for whole-survey recipes.

params.name: unmapped_channels
params.description: What to do about a channel the mapping does not cover, which happens when no calibration file matched it. "warn" (the default) reports the channel on the terminal and falls back to the values the raw file itself records, which is what echopype would calibrate that channel with given no calibration file at all. "error" stops the run instead. The fallback needs the echodata input; without it "warn" raises the way "error" would.

params.name: output_logs_folder
params.description: Where the fallback writes its calibration flags. A temporary folder is used when omitted, which is what a per-file chain wants: several files falling back at once would otherwise race on one flags file.

outputs.name: cal_params
outputs.description: Calibration parameters keyed by channel (gain_correction, sa_correction, EBA)

outputs.name: env_params
outputs.description: Environmental parameters keyed by channel (sound_speed, sound_absorption)

outputs.name: other_params
outputs.description: Additional extracted calibration metadata keyed by channel and source file details. Its unmapped_channels entry names the channels that fell back to the raw file's own recorded values, and is empty when the mapping covered every channel.

nodes.description:
Compute volume backscattering strength (Sv) from raw EchoData. When cal_params and env_params are supplied they are applied to the computation. When omitted, echopype uses default environmental and calibration values embedded in the raw file.
This step is echopype.calibrate.compute_Sv called directly, so the calibration model and its defaults are echopype's.

inputs.name: echodata
inputs.description: Raw EchoData to calibrate, normally the single survey-wide object from combine_raw_files.

inputs.name: cal_params
inputs.description: Optional calibration parameter overrides. When null, echopype uses values from the raw file.

inputs.name: env_params
inputs.description: Optional environmental parameter overrides. When null, echopype uses values from the raw file.

outputs.name: ds_Sv
outputs.description: xarray Dataset containing Sv variable and ping_time, range_sample coordinates

nodes.description:
Compute per-ping transducer depth in metres below the water surface from the EK Platform group, for feeding ``ep_add_depth`` as its ``depth_offset``.
Reads the Platform group directly rather than going through ``ep_add_depth(use_platform_vertical_offsets=true)``, which gets the sign wrong on both EK families for different reasons.
On an EK80 drop keel vessel the transducers ride on a retractable keel and ``drop_keel_offset`` records how far it was lowered, while the ``transducer_offset_z`` and ``water_level`` fields echopype's formula reads are left at zero. echopype carries ``drop_keel_offset`` for provenance and never reads it.
An EK60 file has no ``drop_keel_offset`` at all, and echopype maps the ER60 per-ping transducer depth into ``water_level``, whose value its formula then subtracts (``transducer_offset_z - (water_level + vertical_offset)``, with ``transducer_offset_z`` zero because the ER60 does not populate it). The transducer comes out above the water surface and every depth is short by twice the draft. This step reads ``water_level`` directly instead.
``drop_keel_offset`` is preferred when both are present; the field actually used is recorded in the output's ``static_offset_field`` attr.
The static position is per file and heave is per ping, so the result is ``static offset + datum_correction_m + heave_sign * vertical_offset``. Heave is interpolated onto ds_Sv's ping_time here, which also means ``ep_add_depth`` passes the array straight through instead of resampling it again with nearest neighbour.
The output is small (one value per ping) and is the record of what vertical reference a run actually used, so checkpointing it is cheap and makes the reference auditable without recomputing Sv.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Calibrated Sv dataset supplying the target ``ping_time`` coordinate.

inputs.name: echodata
inputs.description: Source EchoData supplying the Platform group.

params.name: datum_correction_m
params.description: Metres added to the static offset to reach depth below the water surface, for when the recorded offset is measured from a hull datum rather than the waterline. Positive pushes the transducer deeper. The default 0.0 takes the recorded offset as already waterline referenced.

params.name: use_heave
params.description: Add the per-ping ``vertical_offset`` (heave) term. False holds the static keel depth on every ping. When the Platform group carries no usable heave the step reports that and falls back to the static depth.

params.name: heave_sign
params.description: Sign applied to ``vertical_offset``. The default 1.0 was determined empirically on HB2407 (EK80, Henry B. Bigelow) by correlating raw heave against the hand-verified EVL seabed line: the correct sign left a 0.14 m residual against 0.75 m for the wrong one. The convention is not recorded in the file attributes and is not the same sign echopype's own platform-vertical-offsets formula uses (that formula is referenced from a hull datum, not drop_keel_offset) - re-verify the same way on a new vessel or instrument setup rather than assuming.

params.name: interp_method
params.description: Interpolation used to put heave on ping_time. Heave is typically sampled several times coarser than the ping rate, so the default linear is preferred over nearest.

outputs.name: transducer_depth
outputs.description: Transducer depth in metres below the surface, shape (ping_time,), on ds_Sv's exact ping_time coordinate. Wire it into ``ep_add_depth``'s ``depth_offset``. Provenance (the static offset and which Platform field it came from, the correction applied, the heave sign and coverage) is recorded in its attrs.

nodes.description:
Add a surface-referenced ``depth`` data variable to an Sv Dataset. This step is echopype.consolidate.add_depth called directly, so the depth computation and its parameters are echopype's. The result preserves all existing variables (including ``echo_range``) and adds ``depth`` on ``(channel, ping_time, range_sample)`` in metres below surface.
Whatever depth-computation technique is selected (constant ``depth_offset``, Platform vertical offsets, Platform/Beam angles, user-supplied ``tilt``) is fully captured in the values of the resulting ``depth`` array, so downstream consumers can treat the dataset as the single source of truth for vertical reference frame without knowing which technique was used.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Calibrated Sv dataset (typically from compute_sv).

inputs.name: echodata
inputs.description: Source EchoData. Required when any of ``use_platform_vertical_offsets``, ``use_platform_angles``, or ``use_beam_angles`` is true.

params.name: depth_offset
params.description: Vertical offset for the transducer position, in metres. Either a constant, or a per-ping DataArray wired from a producer step such as ``compute_transducer_depth`` (echopype accepts both on this argument; a DataArray must have exactly one dimension and is aligned to ping_time). When set, takes precedence over Platform vertical offsets. Left untyped because the two accepted forms are a scalar and a DataArray.

params.name: tilt
params.description: Constant transducer tilt; 0 corresponds to a vertically-pointing transducer. When set, takes precedence over Platform/Beam angles.

params.name: downward
params.description: True when transducers point downward (typical hull-mounted).

params.name: use_platform_vertical_offsets
params.description: Use Echodata Platform group vertical offsets to compute transducer depth. EK60/EK80 only. Ignored when ``depth_offset`` is set.

params.name: use_platform_angles
params.description: Use Echodata Platform group angles to compute echo_range scaling. EK60/EK80 only. Cannot be combined with ``use_beam_angles``.

params.name: use_beam_angles
params.description: Use Echodata Beam group angles to compute echo_range scaling. EK60/EK80 only. Cannot be combined with ``use_platform_angles``.

outputs.name: ds_Sv
outputs.description: Input Sv dataset with an added ``depth`` variable.

nodes.description:
Trim trailing range samples that carry no data. A raw file records to the sonar's configured range, so after seafloor masking the deep end of ``range_sample`` is entirely NaN. Those samples still cost memory and time in every downstream step, and they widen the binned cell grid that ``compute_mvbs`` and ``compute_per_cell_statistics`` build - the flox reduction behind the latter allocates dense bookkeeping sized by channels x ping bins x range bins, so an over-wide range axis is what pushes it into a MemoryError on a long survey.
A standalone step rather than a parameter on ``apply_sv_mask``, for the same reason ``rechunk_dataset`` is standalone: masking is ping-local and runs correctly per file, but the crop point is a property of the whole survey. Cropping per file would leave the segments with different ``range_sample`` lengths, and the ping_time concatenation resolves that by padding the short ones back out with NaN - which undoes the crop and leaves NaN in ``echo_range``, where downstream range binning reads it. Place this after the fan-in instead.
Three criteria are available and compose - whichever are active each produce a candidate cut and the shallowest wins:
* ``outlier_sigma`` rejects anomalous pings and then crops to the deepest
  **retained** ping. Prefer this survey-wide: a single glitch ping reaching
  far past the seafloor otherwise holds the whole range axis open, which is
  exactly what defeats the lossless mode. The threshold is deliberately
  generous, so uncommon-but-real depths survive and only wild outliers go.
* ``max_range_m`` is a hard ceiling, applied whether or not samples above it
  hold data. Cheapest when the answer is already known (e.g. from the
  deepest point in the survey's seabed lines).
* ``drop_trailing_all_nan`` is the lossless fallback used when no outlier
  test is requested.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Sv Dataset to crop, normally after apply_sv_mask so the seafloor returns are already NaN. Place this after any per-file fan-in, since the crop point is a property of the whole survey.

params.name: max_range_m
params.description: Explicit cap. Range samples deeper than this are dropped whether or not they hold data, so a cap shallower than the deepest echo of interest discards it. Leave unset to derive the crop from the data.

params.name: outlier_sigma
params.description: Standard deviations above the mean, over the per-ping deepest finite sample, at which a ping becomes a candidate outlier. Combined with outlier_margin to form the reject threshold. Leave unset to disable outlier rejection and fall back to drop_trailing_all_nan.

params.name: outlier_margin
params.description: Multiplier applied to (mean + outlier_sigma * sd) to get the reject threshold. Raise it to flag fewer pings, lower it to flag more. The default 1.5 is deliberately loose: on HB2407's 2024-10-15 window it puts the threshold at 424 m against a deepest retained ping of 214 m, so it catches only genuine anomalies. Only used when outlier_sigma is set.

params.name: drop_trailing_all_nan
params.description: Crop to one past the deepest range sample holding a finite Sv value anywhere in the dataset. Lossless. Ignored when outlier_sigma is set. Set false with the other two criteria unset to disable the step without removing it from the recipe.

params.name: data_var
params.description: Variable inspected for finite values.

params.name: range_var
params.description: Variable supplying each sample's range in metres.

outputs.name: ds_Sv
outputs.description: The same Dataset with the trailing empty range samples dropped, so every downstream step works on a narrower range axis.

nodes.description:
Narrow a Dataset to a ping_time window. The user-facing entry point into a survey-wide Sv store: a survey-level recipe computes and checkpoints Sv once for the whole cruise, and a user recipe reuses that checkpoint and calls this to work on its own segment.
Cheap on a zarr-backed Dataset. ``sel`` narrows the dask graph to the chunks the window touches, so only those are read - measured on a 39570-ping store with 3305-ping chunks, a 4001-ping window read 4 of 24 partitions in 1.5 s and 1.4 GB against 16.5 s and 8.9 GB for the whole array. Chunk the survey store along ping_time (see ``rechunk_dataset``) at roughly the window size users ask for.
PLACEMENT MATTERS. Step hashes are a Merkle chain: each step folds in its parents' hashes. Wiring a user's window into an upstream step's params - for example ``initial_setup``'s file_time_start - changes that step's hash and every hash below it, so no two windows ever share a cached Sv. Keep the window on this step, downstream of everything whose checkpoint you want shared, and give the survey-level steps a fixed survey-wide window instead.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Dataset carrying a ping_time coordinate, normally the merged survey Sv loaded from a shared checkpoint.

params.name: start
params.description: Inclusive ISO datetime lower bound (e.g. "2024-10-15T13:38:52"). Leave unset to leave the start open.

params.name: end
params.description: Inclusive ISO datetime upper bound. Leave unset to leave the end open. The step fails rather than returning an empty Dataset when the window selects no pings.

params.name: window
params.description:
Mapping supplying start and end instead of passing them directly. Mutually exclusive with them: giving both is an error rather than a silent precedence rule.
This is the form a mapped fan-out needs. ${_item} is an all-or-nothing token with no attribute access - there is no ${_item.start} - so a step mapped over a list of window dicts cannot pull the two bounds out of the item as separate params and has to take the dict itself. Wire it as ``window: ${_item}``.
Extra keys are ignored, so one dict can carry everything an instance needs (a label, its line files, its raw file list) while this step reads only the bounds. An optional ``label`` key is printed to identify the instance in the run log.

params.name: dim
params.description: Time coordinate to slice. Binned products carry the bin's left edge under a different name, so a compute_per_cell_statistics dataset is windowed with "cell_ping_time" while raw Sv uses the default. The coordinate has to be datetime-valued either way, which the cell grid's left edges are.

params.name: windows
params.description:
Several window dicts at once, each with ``start`` and ``end`` as the single ``window`` form takes. Keeps every ping inside at least one of them, in time order, each ping once even where windows overlap.
This is how a step mapped over the survey's per-file Sv pulls a whole set of dive windows out of each file in one pass: the instance sees one file and cannot loop over the list itself. Wire it straight from the planner, ``windows: ${plan_dives.windows}``, and pair it with ``allow_empty: true`` so the files no window touches drop out at the fan-in. Mutually exclusive with ``window`` and ``start``/``end``.

params.name: snap_to_bin
params.description:
Bin width such as "10s". Widens every window outward to whole bins of that width before selecting: the start moves back to its bin's left edge and the end forward to the last instant of its bin.
Set it to the downstream ping_time_bin when this selection feeds compute_mvbs. A window cut at its exact bounds leaves the first and last bins averaged over only part of their pings, and a window that ends just inside a bin can leave that bin with no ping at all, so the grid comes out one bin short. A later selection on the binned grid still trims to the true window.

params.name: allow_empty
params.description:
Return nothing instead of failing when the window selects no pings.
This is what lets the step be mapped over a whole survey's per-file Sv rather than applied to one merged store. Most files lie outside any one window, and ``merge_datasets`` drops the empty instances when it collects, so the fan-in keeps exactly the files the window touches. That is the route to a windowed analysis that reuses the per-file checkpoints without a survey-wide merge ever being built.
Left false by default: against a single merged store, a window that selects nothing is a mistake and should fail loudly.

outputs.name: ds_Sv
outputs.description: The ping_time slice of the input, lazy when the input is lazy. ``None`` when the window selects no pings and ``allow_empty`` is set.

nodes.description: Build a surface-interference mask from baseline Sv using a selectable method.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Sv Dataset the mask is shaped to. Supplies the range variable each sample's depth is read from.

params.name: surface_depth_m
params.description: Depth above which samples are masked out, removing the transmit pulse ringdown and near-surface bubble layer. The default of 0.0 masks nothing.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Boolean mask DataArray; True means valid data

nodes.description: Build a mask that excludes selected frequency channels. Implementation can be swapped to use different exclusion criteria.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Sv Dataset the mask is shaped to. Supplies the nominal channel frequencies matched against frequencies_to_mask.

params.name: frequencies_to_mask
params.description: Nominal channel frequencies to exclude, as numbers in kHz (e.g. [70, 120, 200]). Every sample on a listed channel is marked invalid and every other channel is left untouched. The default empty list masks nothing.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Boolean mask DataArray; True means valid data

nodes.description:
Read a seafloor line from an Echoview ``.evl`` line file and align it to the Sv dataset's pings, returning a 1-D (ping_time,) DataArray in metres. Use it when a hand-verified Echoview bottom line is more trustworthy than running detection over the Sv data.
Echoview exports a survey as a series of part-day line files, so ``evl_path`` may be a folder: the files whose names span ``file_time_start`` to ``file_time_end`` are selected and concatenated into one line before interpolation. Give it the same window that selected the raw files.
Drop-in swap with the ``detect_seafloor`` and ``ep_detect_seafloor`` ops: the output port name (``seafloor_depth``) and shape (1-D, ping_time) match, so downstream steps such as ``create_seafloor_mask`` work unchanged. The recipe step's ``inputs`` drop the ``echodata`` line (no detection is run) and the ``params`` block takes ``evl_path`` plus the alignment settings below instead of ``channel`` / ``min_valid_depth_m`` or ``method`` / ``method_params``.
Pings the line does not cover come back as NaN, and ``create_seafloor_mask`` rejects **every sample** of a ping whose seafloor is NaN (the metres-vs-metres comparison is False against NaN). The step therefore prints its ping coverage on every run; set ``min_coverage`` to turn a shortfall into a hard error, or widen ``edge_extend_s`` / ``max_gap_s`` if the gaps are benign.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Calibrated Sv dataset supplying the target ``ping_time`` coordinate. Also supplies the vertical reference: pass a dataset that has been through ``ep_add_depth`` so the line can be matched to ``depth`` (metres below the surface), which is what an Echoview seabed line normally records.

params.name: evl_path
params.description:
A single Echoview ``.evl`` line file, or a folder of them to select from with file_time_start / file_time_end. May be a local path or a remote fsspec URL (e.g. gs://bucket/survey/seabed_lines); remote files are read in place (no download) since line files are small. The must_exist check is skipped at validation time for remote URLs and enforced by the step at run time instead.
Mutually exclusive with ``window``: exactly one of the two is required.

params.name: window
params.description:
Mapping carrying the line path under ``window_key``, used instead of ``evl_path``.
This is the form a mapped fan-out needs. ${_item} is an all-or-nothing token with no attribute access - there is no ${_item.seabed_evl} - so a step mapped over a list of window dicts cannot pull the path out of the item as its own param and has to take the dict. Wire it as ``window: ${_item}``.
A window also supplies file_time_start / file_time_end when those are not given directly, so a folder of part-day seabed exports narrows to the window without repeating its bounds. Extra keys are ignored, and an optional ``label`` names the instance in errors.
Note that a window's path is NOT content-fingerprinted the way evl_path is: it arrives as a runtime value rather than a declared param, so re-exporting that line does not by itself invalidate the step. The upstream step that produced the window is what carries its identity.

params.name: window_key
params.description: Key the line path is read from when ``window`` is given. Defaults to "seabed_evl", which is what plan_dive_datasets emits.

params.name: vertical_reference
params.description: What the EVL depths are measured from. "surface" (the default, and Echoview's usual seabed-line reference) means metres below the water surface; "transducer" means metres along the beam from the transducer face. The line is converted to whichever reference ds_Sv carries - depth when ep_add_depth ran upstream, otherwise echo_range.

params.name: min_status
params.description: Drop line points whose Echoview status is below this value (0 = none, 1 = unverified, 2 = bad, 3 = good). When null (the default) every point is kept. Dropped points leave a gap in the line, subject to max_gap_s.

params.name: max_gap_s
params.description: Widest hole in the line, in seconds, to interpolate across; pings sitting inside a wider hole come back as NaN. A ping landing exactly on a line point always keeps that point's depth. When null (the default) holes of any width are interpolated across.

params.name: edge_extend_s
params.description: How many seconds past the line's first and last point to hold that point's depth. The default 0.0 does no extrapolation at all, so pings outside the line's time span are NaN - this is what keeps a line covering only part of a survey from silently asserting a constant seafloor over the rest. Set null to hold the end depths indefinitely.

params.name: depth_offset_m
params.description: Constant metres added to the line, for when the transducer draft configured in Echoview differs from the one baked into ds_Sv['depth']. Positive pushes the seafloor deeper.

params.name: min_coverage
params.description: Fraction of pings (0-1) that must end up with a finite seafloor depth; below it the step fails instead of silently masking the uncovered pings away. Default 0.0 never fails.

params.name: file_time_start
params.description:
Optional inclusive ISO datetime (e.g. "2024-10-12T00:15") selecting which line files in an evl_path folder to read, by the d{YYYYMMDD}_t{HHMMSS}-t{HHMMSS} span in their names. Pass the same window that selected the raw files so the line and the pings stay in step.
A file's span runs from its own name stamp to the *next* file's, not to the end stamp in its own name - Echoview's end stamp under-reports the line's real last point by about one raw file's duration, so trusting it would drop the export straddling the window start and leave the leading pings with no seafloor. Selection is name-based, so no line data is read (or downloaded) to filter. Ignored when evl_path names a single file.

params.name: file_time_end
params.description: Optional inclusive ISO datetime upper bound for line file selection. See file_time_start.

outputs.name: seafloor_depth
outputs.description: Seafloor depth in metres, shape (ping_time,), on ds_Sv's exact ping_time coordinate. Always 1-D (no channel dimension), matching the output of the ``detect_seafloor`` and ``ep_detect_seafloor`` ops so downstream masking steps are interchangeable. NaN wherever the line does not cover a ping.

nodes.description: Build a seafloor mask from baseline Sv and detected seafloor depth. The seafloor depth is passed as an explicit input, enabling swappable detection methods without modifying masking logic.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Sv Dataset the mask is shaped to. Supplies the meter-valued range variable that each sample's depth is compared against.

inputs.name: seafloor_depth
inputs.description: Seafloor depth per ping, shape (ping_time,), from detect_seafloor, ep_detect_seafloor, or read_seafloor_line. Pings where this is NaN produce no valid samples, so an undetected stretch is masked out entirely rather than guessed at.

params.name: seafloor_buffer_m
params.description: Height above the detected seafloor line to also mask out. Widens the exclusion zone to cover detection error and the near-bottom dead zone, at the cost of discarding real backscatter just above the bottom.

params.name: range_var
params.description: Name of the meter-valued variable on ds_Sv to compare against the seafloor line. Must use the same vertical reference as the seafloor line. When null (the default), auto-selects "depth" if present on ds_Sv (i.e., add_depth was run upstream), otherwise falls back to "echo_range".

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Boolean DataArray shaped like ds_Sv['Sv']; True means valid data (above seafloor)

nodes.description: Combine two or more mask datasets into one final mask. Accepts a list of mask inputs to support inserting additional custom mask-producing steps into the chain without changing core framework code.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: List of boolean mask DataArrays to combine

params.name: mode
params.description: Combination mode: 'and' (all must be valid) or 'or' (any must be valid)

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Combined boolean mask DataArray

nodes.description:
Apply a boolean mask to an Sv Dataset, setting masked samples to NaN.
Thin wrapper over echopype.mask.apply_mask, calling it against the Sv variable with NaN as the fill value. It adds nothing of its own, so the broadcasting and alignment rules are echopype's.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Sv Dataset to mask, normally straight from compute_sv.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Boolean mask broadcastable against ds_Sv["Sv"], where True marks a sample to keep. Normally the single mask from combine_masks, so every exclusion rule the recipe built is applied in one pass.

outputs.name: ds_Sv
outputs.description: Sv Dataset with masked samples set to NaN

nodes.description:
Estimate and remove background noise from Sv using the De Robertis and Higginbottom method. Returns a cleaned Sv Dataset.
Thin wrapper over echopype.clean.remove_background_noise. Every parameter below is forwarded to it unchanged, so its behavior is echopype's. The one thing the wrapper adds is that the corrected values are copied over the Sv variable, so downstream steps reading Sv get the cleaned data without having to know about Sv_corrected. Both variables are present on the result.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Sv Dataset to denoise, normally the masked Sv from apply_sv_mask so the seafloor and surface returns are not folded into the noise estimate.

params.name: ping_num
params.description: Number of pings used to estimate the noise level

params.name: range_sample_num
params.description: Number of range samples used to estimate the noise level

params.name: background_noise_max
params.description: Upper limit on the estimated noise level (e.g. '-125dB'); omit to leave it unbounded

params.name: SNR_threshold
params.description: Signal-to-noise ratio below which corrected samples are masked out (e.g. '3.0dB')

outputs.name: ds_Sv
outputs.description: Noise-corrected Sv Dataset

nodes.description: Remove spatiotemporal bins with fewer valid samples than a threshold, reducing noise in MVBS computation.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Sv Dataset to screen, normally the noise-removed Sv from remove_background_noise. Masking has already emptied parts of the grid, which is what leaves some bins with too few samples to average.

params.name: range_bin
params.description: Range bin size (e.g. '2m')

params.name: ping_time_bin
params.description: Ping-time bin size (e.g. '10s')

params.name: nan_threshold
params.description: Fraction of NaN values above which a bin is masked (0.0 to 1.0)

params.name: range_var
params.description: Meter-valued variable to bin along, which must match the value given to compute_mvbs and compute_per_cell_statistics or the sparse mask lands on a different grid than the one it is meant to clean. 'echo_range' measures from the transducer face, 'depth' from the surface and needs the dataset to carry a depth variable. The bin edges are read from the first ping of the first channel, so a range variable that varies from ping to ping, as depth does under platform vertical offsets, is approximated by its first ping.

outputs.name: ds_Sv
outputs.description: The same Dataset with samples in under-populated bins set to NaN. Feed this to compute_mvbs using the same bin sizes.

nodes.description:
Compute Mean Volume Backscattering Strength by averaging Sv over range and time bins. Returns a gridded MVBS Dataset.
This step is echopype.commongrid.compute_MVBS called directly, so the bin edges and the averaging (in the linear domain, converted back to dB) are echopype's.
Every sample is assigned to a bin by the value of its range variable rather than by its range_sample index, so channels recorded at different sample intervals land in the same physical bins. This is what makes MVBS safe for arithmetic across channels on data whose channels do not share a geometry.
The flox_kwargs passthrough echopype accepts is not exposed, since a params block can only supply named arguments.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Cleaned Sv Dataset to average. Normally the output of mask_sparse_bins, so bins that failed the sparsity check are already NaN and do not pull the bin means toward the noise floor.

params.name: range_bin
params.description: Depth bin size for averaging (e.g. '2m')

params.name: ping_time_bin
params.description: Ping-time bin size for averaging (e.g. '10s')

params.name: range_var
params.description: Variable to bin along: 'echo_range' for range from the transducer face, or 'depth' for depth below the surface. 'depth' requires the dataset to carry a depth variable, which ep_add_depth adds; binning by it is what puts channels mounted at different depths on one vertical reference.

params.name: range_var_max
params.description: Deepest value the bins cover, as a unit string (e.g. '2100m'). When unset, echopype reads the maximum from the data, which forces a compute on a lazy dataset. Supplying it keeps the step lazy.

params.name: closed
params.description: Which side of each bin interval is closed: 'left' or 'right'

params.name: skipna
params.description: Skip NaN values when averaging. When false, any NaN in a bin makes the whole bin NaN, so masked data collapses.

params.name: fill_value
params.description: Value for bins holding no data to aggregate. echopype defaults to NaN, which YAML cannot express here, so leaving this unset keeps that default.

params.name: method
params.description: Flox reduction strategy for dask arrays, normally 'map-reduce'. Any other value requires reindex to be set to null in the same params block, since echopype rejects a non-null reindex outside map-reduce and its own default for reindex is false rather than null.

params.name: reindex
params.description: Reindex at the blockwise stage rather than after it. False uses less memory and more time. Only meaningful when method is 'map-reduce'.

outputs.name: ds_MVBS
outputs.description: Gridded MVBS Dataset

nodes.description: Compute per-MVBS-cell statistics (e.g. coefficient of variation) from fine-resolution Sv data before masking or MVBS averaging. Results are stored as new DataArrays in the returned dataset at MVBS-bin resolution. Must be called with the same range_bin, ping_time_bin and range_var values used by mask_sparse_bins and compute_mvbs so that bin grids align exactly. Pass the returned dataset to add_auxiliary_features via the ds_sv input to absorb the statistics into the ML feature matrix.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Fine-resolution Sv Dataset to summarize, normally the noise-removed Sv from remove_background_noise. Take it from before mask_sparse_bins: the within-cell spread is the signal here, and dropping sparse bins first would hide the cells whose variability is most informative.

params.name: range_bin
params.description: Range bin size. Must match mask_sparse_bins and compute_mvbs (e.g. '2m')

params.name: ping_time_bin
params.description: Ping-time bin size. Must match mask_sparse_bins and compute_mvbs (e.g. '10s')

params.name: statistics
params.description: List of statistics to compute. Supported: ['cv']

params.name: data_var
params.description: Name of the Sv variable in the input Dataset

params.name: range_var
params.description: Meter-valued variable to bin along, which must match the value given to mask_sparse_bins and compute_mvbs or the cell statistics describe cells offset from the MVBS cells they are joined to. 'echo_range' measures from the transducer face, 'depth' from the surface and needs the dataset to carry a depth variable. The cell dimension names stay cell_ping_time and cell_echo_range either way, since add_auxiliary_features selects on them by name.

params.name: range_var_max
params.description:
Deepest value the cells cover, as a unit string (e.g. '1810m'), matching the value given to compute_mvbs.
When unset the extent is read from the data. That forces a compute on a lazy dataset, and it lets each dataset choose its own cell grid length, which is only safe when this step runs once on one merged dataset. Mapped over a survey's per-file Sv it is the bug: each file bins to its own extent and the fan-in outer-joins cell_echo_range and NaN-pads the short ones, the same trap the survey tier guards against on range_sample.
Pin it whenever the results will be merged.

params.name: cells_only
params.description:
Return only the statistic arrays instead of a copy of ds_Sv carrying them.
The default keeps the source variables, which is what a single call on a merged dataset wants. Set it true whenever this step is checkpointed or its results are merged: otherwise the fine-resolution Sv is written a second time, and a merge on cell_ping_time drags ping_time and range_sample into the join, which across files with differing range_sample lengths outer-joins and NaN-pads them. That is the same trap the survey tier exists to avoid, reintroduced one dimension over.

outputs.name: ds_Sv
outputs.description: Input Dataset with per-cell statistic variables appended (e.g. cell_cv with dims channel x cell_ping_time x cell_echo_range)

nodes.description: Reconsolidate a collected list of xarray Datasets into a single Dataset by concatenating along a dimension. This is the recipe system's fan-in (collect) target for segment-parallel work: a mapped step that produces one Dataset per data segment (e.g. per-file MVBS) is gathered via ``collect`` and merged back into one Dataset along ``dim`` (default ``ping_time``). A single Dataset passes through unchanged (single-item transparency).

inputs.name: datasets
inputs.description: Collected list of Datasets (one per mapped/swept instance), supplied by a ``collect: ${mapped_step.output}`` directive on the recipe step.

params.name: dim
params.description: Dimension to concatenate the collected Datasets along.

params.name: on_duplicate
params.description:
What to do when two collected segments carry the same label on ``dim``.
Unset (the default) leaves both, which is right when segments cannot overlap - per-file Sv concatenated on raw ping_time, for instance.
"mean" averages them into one entry. That is what a fan-in over per segment BINNED products needs: compute_mvbs and compute_per_cell_statistics anchor their time bins to a global origin, so a segment boundary falling inside a bin makes the segment on each side emit that bin, each holding part of its pings. Left alone the merged store carries a duplicate index, which every downstream reindex rejects - add_auxiliary_features raises InvalidIndexError on it.
"first" keeps the first entry for a label and sorts the result. That is what a fan-in over overlapping SLICES OF ONE STORE needs: dive windows cut from the survey grid, where two dives sharing a minute are the same cells twice, so nothing should be averaged. A per-segment variable that differs on the overlap is kept from the first segment only, which is the sign it does not belong on the shared axis; attach it per segment after the fan-in.
Variables carrying "units: dB" are averaged in the linear domain and converted back, since a mean of decibels is not the mean of what they measure. The average is unweighted: the partial bins do not record how many pings each held.

outputs.name: merged
outputs.description: Single concatenated result, matching the collected element type: a Dataset for collected Datasets, a DataArray for collected DataArrays (e.g. a per-file detect_seafloor line collected into a survey-wide one).

nodes.description: Rechunk a Dataset along ping_time. A standalone step rather than a parameter on any particular masking or reduction op, so a recipe can insert (or remove) chunking wherever a downstream op should run dask-parallel, independent of which step happens to run immediately before it.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Dataset to rechunk. Any Sv-like Dataset is accepted, whatever step produced it.

params.name: ping_time_chunk
params.description: Target chunk size along ping_time.

outputs.name: ds_Sv
outputs.description: The same Dataset backed by dask arrays chunked along ping_time, so the steps wired after it can run chunk-parallel.

nodes.description: Reconsolidate a collected list of xarray Datasets into a single Dataset by concatenating along a dimension. This is the recipe system's fan-in (collect) target for segment-parallel work: a mapped step that produces one Dataset per data segment (e.g. per-file MVBS) is gathered via ``collect`` and merged back into one Dataset along ``dim`` (default ``ping_time``). A single Dataset passes through unchanged (single-item transparency).

inputs.name: datasets
inputs.description: Collected list of Datasets (one per mapped/swept instance), supplied by a ``collect: ${mapped_step.output}`` directive on the recipe step.

params.name: dim
params.description: Dimension to concatenate the collected Datasets along.

params.name: on_duplicate
params.description:
What to do when two collected segments carry the same label on ``dim``.
Unset (the default) leaves both, which is right when segments cannot overlap - per-file Sv concatenated on raw ping_time, for instance.
"mean" averages them into one entry. That is what a fan-in over per segment BINNED products needs: compute_mvbs and compute_per_cell_statistics anchor their time bins to a global origin, so a segment boundary falling inside a bin makes the segment on each side emit that bin, each holding part of its pings. Left alone the merged store carries a duplicate index, which every downstream reindex rejects - add_auxiliary_features raises InvalidIndexError on it.
"first" keeps the first entry for a label and sorts the result. That is what a fan-in over overlapping SLICES OF ONE STORE needs: dive windows cut from the survey grid, where two dives sharing a minute are the same cells twice, so nothing should be averaged. A per-segment variable that differs on the overlap is kept from the first segment only, which is the sign it does not belong on the shared axis; attach it per segment after the fan-in.
Variables carrying "units: dB" are averaged in the linear domain and converted back, since a mean of decibels is not the mean of what they measure. The average is unweighted: the partial bins do not record how many pings each held.

outputs.name: merged
outputs.description: Single concatenated result, matching the collected element type: a Dataset for collected Datasets, a DataArray for collected DataArrays (e.g. a per-file detect_seafloor line collected into a survey-wide one).

inputs.name: ds_MVBS
inputs.description: Gridded MVBS Dataset to flatten, from compute_mvbs, or from add_line_overlay when a line variable should travel with it. One MVBS cell becomes one ML sample, with the channels of that cell as its features.

params.name: data_var
params.description: Name of the data variable to use as features

params.name: dataset_name
params.description: Name this ML dataset is stored under inside the returned Dataset. Every later ML step (add_auxiliary_features, normalize_ml_data, run_hdbscan, the ML plots) takes the same dataset_name to find the feature matrix again, so a recipe can carry several independent ML datasets side by side.

params.name: feature_strategy
params.description: Feature construction strategy (e.g. 'mean_centered')

params.name: baseline_channel
params.description: Channel index used as the baseline when computing relative features

outputs.name: ds_ml_ready
outputs.description: Flattened ML-ready Dataset

nodes.description: Append auxiliary coordinate-derived features (e.g. depth, ping_time_seconds) to the flattened ML-ready Dataset. Optional step; omit when no auxiliary features are needed.

inputs.name: ds_ml
inputs.description: Flattened ML Dataset from reshape_for_ml. The new features are appended as extra columns on its feature matrix.

inputs.name: echodata
inputs.description: Raw EchoData supplying the echosounder's own bottom pick, used for the 'seafloor_depth' and 'altitude' features when the seafloor_depth input is not wired. Ignored when it is.

inputs.name: ds_sv
inputs.description: Dataset returned by compute_per_cell_statistics, carrying per-MVBS-cell statistic variables (e.g. cell_cv). Required when 'cell_cv' is listed in features.

inputs.name: seafloor_depth
inputs.description:
Pre-detected seafloor line, 1-D over ping_time, typically wired from a detect_seafloor step. Takes precedence over echodata for the 'seafloor_depth' and 'altitude' features, so the ML features use the same line the masking stack used instead of a channel mean recomputed internally. Either this or echodata is required for those features.
In a per-file map_over pipeline, collect the per-file lines into one survey-wide line and wire that, e.g. a merge_datasets step with collect: ${detect_seafloor.seafloor_depth}. This input does accept the raw list of per-file lines and concatenates it along ping_time in segment order, but a recipe cannot reference a mapped step from outside its chain and still resume: the runner prunes a mapped chain as a whole once the downstream fan-in is a cache hit, so the direct reference resolves on a cold run and fails on a resumed one.
Vertical reference: 'altitude' is a difference (seafloor minus sample), so a constant offset shared by both terms cancels and the frame does not matter as long as they agree. They normally do: detect_seafloor promotes its line to surface-referenced only when its ds_Sv carries depth, the same condition under which depth reaches the ML dataset, and 'altitude' prefers depth over echo_range to pair with it.

params.name: dataset_name
params.description: ML dataset to append the features to. Must match the dataset_name used by reshape_for_ml.

params.name: features
params.description: List of built-in feature name strings to append. Supported built-ins: 'depth', 'ping_time_seconds', 'seafloor_depth', 'altitude', 'cell_cv'. 'seafloor_depth' and 'altitude' require the echodata input. 'cell_cv' requires the ds_sv input (from compute_per_cell_statistics).

outputs.name: ds_ml_ready
outputs.description: ML-ready Dataset with auxiliary features appended

params.name: method
params.description: Global normalization method (e.g. 'flatten', 'minmax', 'zscore')

params.name: dataset_name
params.description: ML dataset to normalize. Must match the dataset_name used by reshape_for_ml.

params.name: normalization_name
params.description: Name this normalized result is stored under. run_hdbscan, the ML plots, and filter_normalized_by_cluster take the same name to find it, so several normalizations of one dataset can coexist and be compared.

params.name: shift_positive
params.description: Shift all values to be non-negative after normalization
